subject: social-studies
title: Landscape Change: The Singapore River Mouth, Stage by Stage

slides.heading: Landscape Change: The Singapore River Mouth, Stage by Stage
bullets: How one place at the mouth of the Singapore River changed over a long time: a fishing village became a trading port, the port grew bigger, and at last a modern city stood on the same shore - one stage at a time, with the people bar climbing at every stage
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we stay at one place - the mouth of the Singapore River - and watch it change slowly, stage by stage, instead of all at once.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain how the landscape at the river mouth changed in stages: fishing village, trading port, bigger port, modern city
Run the change in order and name what was built and who arrived at each stage
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to tell the whole story of this one place in the right order.

slides.heading: The village is gone and a city is here - did it change overnight?
bullets: Old pictures show huts and small fishing boats at this shore; today there are tall buildings, roads and container ships
Did the city replace the village in one sudden jump, or did the place change little by little?
slides.notes: Ask the class: when two pictures look completely different, does that mean the change happened all at once? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation walks through every stage in between.

slides.heading: Landscapes change gradually, stage by stage
bullets: A landscape changes when people build new things in a place over a long time - here, growing trade brought godowns, a jetty, warehouses and at last tall buildings
Each stage grows out of the stage before it: more trade meant more work, and more work brought more people
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: stage by stage, not in one jump - every new building answers a need created by the stage before it.

slides.heading: Stage 1: a fishing village at the river mouth
bullets: A few families live in huts at the river mouth and fish from small boats
The people bar is tiny: very few people live here in the village stage
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the huts, the small boats and the tiny people bar: this is the starting picture of the same shore.

slides.heading: Stage 2: trade grows and a port is built
bullets: More ships come to trade, so godowns are built to store goods and a jetty reaches into the water
More people arrive to work at the busy port, and the people bar climbs
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the change: trade grows first, then the godowns and jetty are built, then more people arrive - cause and effect in order.

slides.heading: Stage 3: the port expands with steamships
bullets: Steamships replace sailing ships, and the port expands with long rows of warehouses
The people bar climbs again as the bigger port offers more work
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and compare the shore with stage 2: same place, bigger port - the change is still happening one stage at a time.

slides.heading: Stage 4: the modern city, built stage by stage
bullets: Today the same shore holds tall buildings, busy roads and container ships, and the people bar is at its highest
The wrong-turn timeline is played out and corrected: village, port, bigger port, city - no stage was skipped
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and run the stage timeline: the city is the last stage of a long, gradual change, not a sudden replacement.

slides.heading: Worked example: telling the story of one shore in order
bullets: Start: a fishing village of huts and small boats, with very few people
Finish: a modern city - reached only after the trading port stage and the expanded port stage in between
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Stage 1, fishing village. Stage 2, trade grows and a port is built. Stage 3, the port expands with steamships. Stage 4, the modern city. At each stage ask: what changed, and what caused it?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the stages in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from the fishing village, name each stage in order and say what was built and how the people bar moved at that stage
Then swap and check: did your partner run every stage in order, or jump straight from the village to the city?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for all four stages in order, then take two pairs answers: fishing village, trading port, expanded port, modern city.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the modern city replaced the fishing village in a single step
Name the stages in between and what caused each change to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers run the stages in order and name growing trade as the driver.
